title: Listening contacts never compose, and a shared chain carries the far ring only after crossing the middle ring
subject: What a chain of three rings joined by two contacts can carry, read with the canonical knot test on its space-time law
conclusion: Three rings in a chain, A and B joined by contact c1 and B and C by contact c2, written as one space-time law; a contact binds two rings when every minimally decisive set of its value meets both rings' own first-row cells. With listening contacts, which read their rings and feed nothing back, the far contact never depends on the far ring, so the chain never binds its ends: composition across time needs a contact that the middle ring reads, the contact gate's shared identity. With shared contacts, c2 does not depend on ring A's first row before lag d + 1, d the distance between the contacts on ring B, so the ends can be bound only from that lag. With linear or affine rules and affine contact laws, a contact binds two rings exactly when the support of its row of M^T meets both.
